AN.title: make A2 decidable while the log is being written

AN.note:
MEASURED 24 Aug 2026. A2 is not failing because replay is broken -- replay reproduces exactly. It fails because `doctor` compares the persisted projection against a replay of the *live* log, and with ~20 agents appending, events land between the two reads. Observed in one sitting, same repository, minutes apart: FAIL ('canonical state diverged'), then UNKNOWN ('state covers N of M events'), then PASS -- the last only because the rebuild and the check happened in the same instant.

So the condition as written is decidable only on a quiet repository, and this repository is never quiet. A gate that reports three different verdicts for one unchanged history is measuring contention, not replay.

Fix it by deciding A2 against a **pinned prefix**: take the projection's own high-water mark, replay exactly that many events, and compare. Events appended after the mark are outside the comparison -- they are not evidence of divergence and must not be reported as such. A genuine mismatch inside the prefix must still FAIL, and an empty prefix must still be UNKNOWN (do not reintroduce the tautological pass repaired on 20 Aug 2026).

The test is the point of this unit: `tests/test_doctor_a2_concurrent.py` must append to the log *while* the check runs and assert the verdict is stable and correct. A test that only runs on a quiet log reproduces the bug it is meant to catch.

Do NOT make A2 pass by widening what counts as identical. The divergence report is right in principle; the read window is what is wrong.

AU.title: narrow the cursor lock to startup so Cursor capacity is usable

AU.note:
MEASURED 24 August 2026. The principal reports Cursor quota at 4% used while Claude and Codex are saturated, and this is why.

`scripts/dispatch.py` wraps the ENTIRE cursor-composer run in ExclusiveFileLock(DEFAULT_CURSOR_LOCK) for the full leash. With a 3600s leash that means one cursor dispatch per hour: extras block their whole leash and then fail with 'cursor-agent lock held'. Three units burned an hour each that way on 24 Aug, and build_driver.py had to add CURSOR_CONCURRENCY = 1 to stop the driver wasting slots on dispatches that could never start.

WHAT THE LOCK PROTECTS, measured: the comment says two cursor-agent processes race `~/.cursor/cli-config.json`. That file contains NO credentials -- only preferences (approvalMode, display, permissions, sandbox, version). Its mtime on 24 Aug was 21 Aug 22:24, THREE DAYS STALE, across dozens of cursor dispatches. So ordinary runs do not write it at all; it is written only when a setting changes.

So the lock's EXISTENCE is defensible and its SCOPE is not: an hour-long exclusive hold protects a file written perhaps weekly, and it costs almost all of a paid quota.

Narrow it to the window where contention is real -- process startup, when the config is read -- and release it once the child is running. Measure where the write actually happens before choosing the boundary; do not guess the number. If cursor-agent turns out to write the config on exit too, say so and cover both ends rather than pretending one is enough.

Then raise CURSOR_CONCURRENCY in .harness/build_driver.py to match what the narrowed lock genuinely allows, and say what you measured it to be.

DO NOT simply delete the lock. A corrupted cli-config.json would break every cursor dispatch at once, and the race is real even if rare. The test must prove two concurrent dispatches can run AND that the config survives them intact.

AV.title: read the cross-family verdict instead of discarding it
AV.commit: fix(driver): consume the review verdict and block retirement on a bad one
AV.note:
MEASURED 24 August 2026, and this is the most beta-adverse defect in the build.

The driver dispatches a cross-family review for every built unit -- a DIFFERENT MODEL FAMILY from the builder, which is the only genuinely different class of evidence in the whole pipeline -- writes the reviewer's output to `<uid>-verify.out`, and then NEVER READS IT. `state["verified"]` is read at build_driver.py:1138 and :1142 and initialised at :1082, and NOTHING WRITES A UNIT INTO IT. The 19 entries currently there came from a hand-run review on 23 Aug, not from the pipeline.

So every review is dispatched, billed against the principal's quota, and discarded. The system performs consilience and throws away the result. Per CONSILIENCE.md the whole project rests on convergence from a different class of facts being a TEST -- a test whose outcome is never read is not a test, and a unit marked done on the builder's say-so alone is exactly the echo this repository exists to refuse.

What to build: parse `<uid>-verify.out` for a structured verdict, record it in `state["verified"]` and in the TRAJECTORY, and make a unit's retirement depend on it. A SOUND verdict retires the unit. A verdict finding blocking defects must PREVENT retirement and put the unit back for repair with the findings attached.

Require the reviewer to emit a machine-readable verdict; do not regex prose for the word 'sound'. An unparseable verdict is NOT a pass -- fail closed, because the whole point is that the absence of evidence stopped being treated as evidence.

Evidence for how strict this should be: the one hand-run cross-family review of 19 units found 0 sound, 5 blocking and 68 surviving findings, and 14 of 19 carried a guard that could be deleted with the suite still green. Reviewed is not sound, and the pipeline currently cannot tell the difference.

Do NOT make the verdict advisory-only to keep throughput up. Throughput through an unmeasured filter is the thing being sold here, and it is worth less than nothing.

PRIORITY 25, set deliberately on 24 August 2026. This unit unblocks nothing, so ordering by downstream impact would dispatch it last. That is backwards: it does not release work, it makes every unit already released trustworthy. Until it lands, 'done' means one model said so.

AR.title: narrow the held-out refusal to brief, worktree and claims, and void a measurement on contract leakage
AR.commit: fix(gate): refuse a held-out contract reachable from brief, worktree or claims
AR.note:
GATE WORK for A1 — ". Specified by the gate-diagnosis workflow on 24 August 2026 after reading the code; every claim in this brief was measured, not assumed.

Read ADR-0103's Enforcement section before touching anything. This unit REPAIRS K01 (commit 46e08ae), it does not undo it.

THE DEFECT, measured 24 August 2026. `.github/scripts/check_heldout_isolation.py` is 24 lines and refuses UNCONDITIONALLY: `refusal_reason()` returns a refusal for any argument and `main()` always returns 2. `scripts/dispatch.py:2500-2508` refuses any `--heldout-contract` before preflight, and its help text at dispatch.py:2458-2460 says 'refused until dispatch gains real isolation'. The consequence is that no held-out contract can be supplied to any dispatch on this architecture, so no contract-beta can be measured, so EXP-142 stays BLOCKED on its precondition and units K02, K03, K04 and AS all have nothing to stand on.

WHY THIS IS A REPAIR AND NOT A RELAXATION, and you must be able to state this yourself before you write a line. ADR-0103's Enforcement specifies the boundary exactly: 'refuses a build dispatch whose brief, worktree or claims can reach the held-out contract for that unit.' K01 refused on a broader ground -- that a same-OS-user unsandboxed child can read any file in principle -- which is true, and which converted the principal's guard into a wall that blocks his own decision. Narrowing to the specified boundary is implementing the decision. It is a relaxation ONLY if you leave the residual open, which is why the second half of this unit is mandatory and not optional.

WHAT TO BUILD.
(a) Make `check_heldout_isolation.py` decide rather than assert. It takes the contract path and the dispatch's brief text, worktree root and declared claims, and refuses when the contract is inside the worktree, named or quoted in the brief, or covered by any claim. It PERMITS otherwise, and prints what it checked. `scripts/dispatch.py` calls it with the real values instead of refusing on the flag's mere presence.
(b) Add a post-build audit mode to the SAME file -- do not create a second script. It reads the child's transcript (`<uid>.out`, `<uid>.err` under `.harness/dispatch/`) and the produced diff, and reports LEAKED if the contract's path, its sha256, or any of its distinctive content lines appear. A leaked measurement is VOID, not merely flagged.
(c) For (b), REUSE `.github/scripts/check_private_corpus.py`'s existing whole-line shingle fingerprinting -- case-folded words, >=12 words and >=80 characters, SHA-256 digests. Do not write a new fingerprinter. This is already in the codebase and it is the same problem.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO. Do not delete the refusal path -- a contract inside the worktree must still be refused before child launch, and `tests/test_heldout_isolation.py::test_heldout_contract_refuses_before_dispatch_preflight` must keep passing in substance. Do not build a container, a second OS user or a WSL uid boundary; that is weeks of Windows work for a residual (b) already covers, and nothing here has been measured to support it. Do not print the contract's contents in any refusal or audit output -- follow `check_private_corpus.py`, which never prints a matched private path in full.

RECORD THE RESIDUAL HONESTLY, in the module docstring: a child that reads the contract and neither echoes its path nor reproduces its assertions is not detected. Tag it `[asserted]`. That sentence is load-bearing for EXP-142's write-up and must not be softened.

DONE WHEN: a dispatch whose worktree, brief or claims can reach the contract is refused with exit 2 before child launch; a dispatch that cannot reach it proceeds; the audit mode returns LEAKED on a transcript containing the contract path, its digest, or a fingerprinted line, and CLEAN otherwise; every assertion above has a test that fails if the behaviour is removed.

AX.title: author a different-family held-out contract from pre-registered intent and commit its digest before dispatch
AX.commit: feat(gate): author a held-out contract from a different family before the build
AX.note:
GATE WORK for A1 — ". Specified by the gate-diagnosis workflow on 24 August 2026 after reading the code; every claim in this brief was measured, not assumed.

This is K02, re-specified against the narrowed K01. It cannot run until unit 1 lands, because dispatch refuses every held-out contract until then.

WHAT MUST EXIST, per ADR-0103's Decision section. The contract is derived from the SAME stated intent as the build, by a DIFFERENT model family from the builder, committed before the build dispatch, and never placed anywhere the builder or its checks can read.

CONCRETELY.
(a) The intent statement is the unit's `title` and `note` from `.harness/plan-units.json`. That is what already exists and it is pre-registered by construction -- do not invent a new intent format.
(b) Author the contract by dispatching to a family different from the one that will build, using the family selection machinery already in `scripts/dispatch.py`. The family difference must be REFUSED AT DISPATCH if violated, not merely logged. ADR-0103 names this as one of its three checks.
(c) Write the contract OUTSIDE the unit worktree and outside anything the claims cover, so unit 1's reachability check passes.
(d) Append a `measurement.registered` trajectory event with `config_hash` = the sha256 of the contract file, BEFORE the build dispatch starts. `src/consilient/events.py:286-336` already validates this event kind and requires 64 lower-case hex; `.github/scripts/check_measurement_recorded.py` already proves CI refuses a result without prior registration. Reuse both. Do not invent a new event kind and do not write the digest into a JSON side-file.

WHY THE DIGEST MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The commitment is what stops the contract being rewritten after the artefact exists to match what the builder did -- Goodhart through the front door, which ADR-0103 names as the thing that would make beta_T measure nothing. Without a pre-committed digest, 'authored before the build' is a claim nobody can check afterwards.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO. Do not let the caller supply the family of either side -- derive the builder's family from the dispatch that will actually run. Do not weaken the refusal in unit 1 to make placement convenient; move the file instead. Do not have the contract-authoring dispatch see the artefact, the builder's brief beyond the intent text, or the repository's own test suite for the claimed paths.

WATCH FOR THE TRIPWIRE, and record it: a contract that never marks a violation is not evidence of quality, it is evidence the contract was written to match what the builder was going to do anyway. The violation rate must be recorded alongside every contract so EXP-142 can report it.

DONE WHEN: a build dispatch for a measured unit refuses unless a contract digest is already in the trajectory and the authoring family differs from the builder's; the contract file sits outside the worktree and outside the claims; and a test fails if either refusal is removed.

AY.title: admit contract_beta as a gate estimand, strictly separate from human-beta and from every proxy
AY.commit: feat(beta): admit contract-beta for the gate, refusing every proxy estimand
AY.note:
GATE WORK for A1 — ". Specified by the gate-diagnosis workflow on 24 August 2026 after reading the code; every claim in this brief was measured, not assumed.

This is K03, re-specified. It deps on AT only because AT already claims `src/consilient/projection.py` and claims are locks -- there is no logical dependency between signed verdicts and contract-beta, and the two code regions do not overlap.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, measured 24 August 2026. `src/consilient/beta.py:39-47` defines `HUMAN_VERDICT_BETA = 'human_verdict_beta'` and `PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS = {mutation_proxy_beta, critic_proxy_beta, repository_consequence_false_shipment_cohort_lower_bound}`. `admits_human_beta_row` (beta.py:183-191) refuses every proxy and requires `auth_status == 'authenticated'`. `projection.py:66-67, 979, 1030-1034, 1141-1145` writes `estimand_kind` and `auth_status` onto outcome rows, and hardcodes `'human_verdict_beta'` at both write sites. Nothing anywhere writes or reads a contract-beta row. Grep for `contract_beta` across src, tests, docs, scripts and .github returns only ADR-0103 and EXP-142 prose.

WHAT TO BUILD.
(a) A `CONTRACT_BETA = 'contract_beta'` estimand kind and an `admits_gate_row()` that admits it and NOTHING else. It must refuse every kind in `PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS`, refuse `human_verdict_beta`, and refuse any row whose `auth_status` is not authenticated.
(b) `admits_human_beta_row` must be left EXACTLY as it is. The two admission rules stay separate functions with separate tests. ADR-0103 is explicit: human-beta is alignment, reported separately, never blocking, and its rule is 'unchanged and continues to refuse every proxy'.
(c) A projection write path that records a contract-beta outcome row: the held-out contract's verdict (violation or not) as the condition, and the project's own checks' verdict (accept or reject) as the outcome. beta_T = P(checks accept | contract violated). The row must carry the repository it was measured on, because A1 reports per repository and pooling is forbidden.
(d) A row whose measurement was marked LEAKED by unit 1's audit must be REFUSED here, not silently included.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO, and this is the whole point of the separation. Do not widen `PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS` and do not admit anything in it into the gate projection. `critic_proxy_beta`, `mutation_proxy_beta` and the repository-consequence lower bound are DIFFERENT ESTIMANDS, not cheaper estimates of the same one -- ADR-0080's algebra is that they 'say nothing about H without labels'. Do not perform the substitution `q_upper := beta_upper` that ADR-0080 forbids. Do not admit a `declared_principal` auth status: `scripts/verdict.py` lets its caller choose the principal, so a local agent process can forge one, and admitting it would let the system fabricate the ground truth used to measure its own error rate.

Do not lower `MIN_REJECTIONS` or add a knob that can lower a floor. beta.py:216-219 already refuses a `min_rejections` below the constant; contract-beta needs its own floor with the same property -- raisable only.

DONE WHEN: `admits_gate_row` admits a clean contract_beta row and refuses each of the four other kinds by name in a test; a leaked row is refused; `admits_human_beta_row`'s behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged and a test proves it; and a Wilson interval is computed per repository with no pooling path available.

AZ.title: gate A1 on contract-beta over two repositories, read from the trajectory rather than a prose regex

AZ.note:
GATE WORK for A1 — ". Specified by the gate-diagnosis workflow on 24 August 2026 after reading the code; every claim in this brief was measured, not assumed.

This supersedes BOTH unit AS and unit K04, which are near-duplicates claiming `src/consilient/cli.py` for the same change on different dep chains. Retire whichever survives; do not run both.

THE DEFECT, measured 24 August 2026. `src/consilient/cli.py:426-484` computes A1 from one input: EXP-01's entry in `docs/10-research/experiment-register.md`. `EXP01_BETA` (cli.py:94-96) matches `beta-measured: p [lo, hi]`; cli.py:433-452 sets `stopping_rule_fired` from the literal string 'stopping rule FIRED' and hard-fails. ADR-0103 is the principal's own decision, dated 23 August 2026, and it moved the gate quantity to contract-beta (beta_T). The decision moved and the code did not follow. Implement his decision; do not invent one.

WHAT TO BUILD.
(a) A1 reads the contract-beta projection from the TRAJECTORY via `admits_gate_row`, not a regex over markdown. Delete the `EXP01_BETA` route from A1 entirely.
(b) A1 requires TWO repositories, each with its own interval, never pooled. (e) Human-beta is reported SEPARATELY and blocks nothing. ADR-0103's reasoning is the principal's own and must be preserved: he is by design a weaker judge of the system's output than the system, so a gate resting on his verdicts measures agreement with the weaker judge rather than correctness.

THE PROSE-EDIT HOLE, which you must close and not reproduce. `tests/test_v0_invariants.py:2871-2885` proves A1 currently reports PASS if someone edits the register to drop 'stopping rule FIRED' while keeping a `beta-measured:` line. Do not admit a proxy estimand; `PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS` exists precisely to keep `critic_proxy_beta`, `mutation_proxy_beta` and the repository-consequence lower bound out of the projection, and that separation stands. Do not make A1 depend on human-beta. Do not make it pass. ADR-0103's Enforcement section says in terms: 'none of these exists today ... Gate A1 must continue to report FAIL. That is stated here so nobody reads this ADR as having opened it.'

DONE WHEN: A1 reports FAIL with a reason naming the ABSENT contract-beta measurement rather than the retired EXP-01 route; a test fails if A1 ever passes without an interval; a test fails if A1 passes on a proxy estimand; a test fails if A1 passes on one repository; a test fails if A1 passes while ADR-0103 is PROVISIONAL; and no A1 code path reads `docs/10-research/experiment-register.md`.

BA.title: Make the canonical state digest independent of where the log lives
BA.commit: fix(projection): digest the log's content, not its absolute path
BA.note:
GATE WORK for A2 — R. Specified by the gate-diagnosis workflow on 24 August 2026 after reading the code; every claim in this brief was measured, not assumed.

THE DEFECT. Gate A2 fails deterministically on this repository, and the state does not diverge. `state_digest` (src/consilient/projection.py:1544) hashes every column of every table, and `rejections.path` (written by `_apply_rejections`, src/consilient/projection.py:279, insert at :291) holds the ABSOLUTE filesystem path of the file a refused line came from — `events.Rejection.path`, src/consilient/events.py:337, populated by `read_all` at :2852. Unit AN's pinned-prefix comparison (landed as 7e9bd0e) must rebuild the prefix in a scratch directory, `db.parent / (db.stem + "-a2-prefix")` at src/consilient/cli.py:321, so every rejection row it produces carries a different path from the persisted one. Any log with at least one refused line therefore reports 'canonical state diverged' forever. This one has six permanent ones (2026-08-20.jsonl lines 62/63/66 baselined by ADR-0043; 2026-08-22.jsonl lines 27/35/45).

THE EVIDENCE. [measured] 24 August 2026, on a frozen copy of `.harness/state.db` (2945 events) and `.harness/log`, reproducing `cmd_replay`'s comparison exactly: persisted digest `58da482c07c766…`, pinned-prefix digest `b6f2804443ef26…`. A per-table digest of both databases: every table identical EXCEPT `rejections`, 6 rows on each side, identical `id`, `line` and `reason` on all six, differing only in `path`. Rewrite `rejections.path` to its basename on both sides, re-digest, and both give `d9438ac950072222…`. A2 passes on this history the moment the path is normalised. Reproduce this before you change anything; if your reproduction disagrees, stop and report rather than proceeding.

WHAT TO DO. Two changes, both small.

1. Store the log-relative name, not the absolute path. In `_apply_rejections`, normalise the value written to `rejections.path` to the daily file's name (the log directory is flat — `read_all` and `_copy_event_prefix` both use `glob("*.jsonl")`). Do NOT change `Rejection.path` itself: it is returned out of `read_all` and used by the dashboard and by `cmd_replay`'s `quarantined` payload, where the full path is wanted. Normalise only at the database boundary. Nothing reads `rejections.path` back out of the database — verify that yourself before you rely on it.

2. Stamp the projection so the one-off change is not misreported as divergence. Adding (1) changes the digest, so the FIRST run after this lands would compare an old-code database against a new-code rebuild and report 'canonical state diverged' — a false failure on the very gate that exists to catch false verdicts, and the same false failure will recur on every future change to `SCHEMA`, `_apply` or `state_digest`. So: add a module constant `PROJECTION_VERSION` in projection.py, bump it in this commit, write it with `PRAGMA user_version = …` in `build` (sqlite has this built in — do NOT add a table; a new table would itself be covered by `state_digest`), read it from the existing database in `cmd_replay` before digesting, and when it differs from the code's constant have `_replay_condition` return status `unknown` with a reason naming both versions. This is the version half of unit AC, which is NOT in HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor c91aa66 HEAD` fails); whoever lands AC later must merge with this rather than revert it.

WHAT MUST NOT BE DONE. Do not touch the prefix pinning — AN is correct and is the reason A2 is decidable at all while the log is being written. Do not widen what counts as identical, do not drop `rejections.path` from the digest (a rejection moving files must still change it), and do not make the version stamp an escape hatch: `PROJECTION_VERSION` is a constant in code, never derived from data or from the database being read, and a version MISMATCH yields `unknown`, never `pass`. A genuine mismatch inside the prefix under the SAME version must still FAIL. Do not reintroduce the tautological pass repaired on 20 August 2026: an empty prefix stays `unknown`. Do not touch `_object_status` (src/consilient/projection.py:1149) — its working-tree dependence is a real latent defect of the same shape, but it is measured NOT to be the cause here (prefix digests with `workspace=REPO` and `workspace=None` are both `b6f2804443ef26…`, and `record_facts` is empty) and it belongs to its own unit.

HOW YOU KNOW YOU ARE FINISHED. (a) tests/test_doctor_a2_concurrent.py gains a case that puts an UNREADABLE line in the log — this is the hole that let the defect through, since none of its five existing tests ever produces a rejection — and asserts A2 is `pass` with the prefix comparison intact. (b) A case asserting a same-version genuine divergence inside the prefix still returns `fail`, and (c) a case asserting a version mismatch returns `unknown`, not `pass` and not `fail`. (d) Run `consil doctor` in this worktree twice in succession: the first run may report A2 `unknown` for the version change, the second must report `pass` with a reason naming 2945-or-more compared events. Report the actual output of both runs; do not claim the gate moved without pasting what doctor said.

THE ADR MUST GET THE CAUSE RIGHT. Two claims in the earlier draft are false and must not be repeated. These three are INTERIOR, with valid lines after them and the file ending cleanly; AB would have caught none of them.
